title: Questions for Prohibitionists, If Cannabis Legalization Is Such A Failure, What Should We Do?
description: The legalization of cannabis has certainly had a variety of problems, too many regulations, too many taxes, too many bureaucratic delays in impleme...
content_html_sanitized:
The legalization of cannabis has certainly had a variety of problems, too many regulations, too many taxes, too many bureaucratic delays in implementation, and the very American boom and bust exuberance, etc…

 

So now there are calls for repealing the various state laws, and???

 

Well, forgive me if I ask for a few specifics, and test everyone’s memory about what we had before this supposed failure.

 

First, Do you know how much cannabis use increased under Prohibition?

 

No one knows how little was being used in 1937, but it was very limited, mostly by Blacks and Hispanics, which is why the laws were easily sold to white politicians.

 

In 2024, approximately 64.1 million people used marijuana in the past year in the U.S. Is  that your idea of a successful policy?

 

Do you know how many Americans have been arrested for simple possession since Nixon escalated the war on cannabis after the Schafer Commission recommended that it be decriminalized?

Approximately, 30 Million Marijuana Arrests and Counting Enough is Enough!

 

And do you know how many Americans were arrested last year?

More Than 200000 People Were Arrested For Marijuana In The U.S. Last Year, FBI Data Shows

Most for simple possession.

 

What should be the penalty for possession? There was — and still is— a wide range of penalties varying from state to state, in the 26 states where recreational marijuana is still illegal.

 

In 1973, before we got the old marijuana laws changed, there were over 800 in the Texas state prisons for possession of less than one ounce! Thirty of them were doing LIFE! And remember that was back when everyone thought that marijuana prohibition was harmless. How do you feel about that?

 

Are you in favor of requiring persons convicted of simple possession be subjected to random urine tests, monitored by someone appointed by the courts? Failure of the test could result in revocation of probation. That has been the policy in many states.

See

Driving to School Is One of the "Extracurricular Activities" That Can Be Used To Justify Random Urine Tests

And

Should parents lose custody of their children for possession of marijuana?

 

Should students lose their scholarships for possession of marijuana?

See

Iowa 7th Graders Reject Opportunity To Win Scholarship For Writing About Hemp – "They objected to the marijuana leaf."

Iowa 7th Graders Reject Opportunity To Win Scholarship For Writing

About Hemp – "They objected to the marijuana leaf."

 

Should sick and dying Americans be allowed access to medical marijuana? How sick should they have to be? Who decides that?

See

Transcript of 1996 Conversation Between the Czar and the Former Managing Editor of New York Times About Medical Marijuana Initiatives Gives Great Insight Into How Marijuana Prohibition Really Works.

 

Should people arrested with marijuana be required to attend and “pass” a court supervised “Drug Education” as a requirement for probation?

See

When The Partnership For A Marijuana-Free America Speaks, The Media For A Marijuana-Free America Parrots. Widely Reported Press Release About Kids and "Drugs" Mentions Marijuana 29 Times, Alcohol 0!

 

Should school students be required to attend “Drug Education” classes taught by the police?

See

NORML Responds to Libels by Houston DARE 2005-03-23

And

How will people be able to know the THC levels in black market weed? How will they be able to know whether it is real cannabis or a dangerous synthetic?

 

So…

 

Just asking!
